text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Malawi opposition parties on Tuesday applied to the High Court to declare that the current sitting of Parliament without the opposition be declared unlawful.

The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) and People's Democratic Party (PDP) applied to the court to also declare that decisions and resolutions passed be declared null and void.
- Civil Servants on Tuesday threatened they will begin a nation-wide strike on Monday, December 23, after a two-year long futile negotiation with government.

Civil Servants Trade Union (CSTU) President Thomas Banda told more than 200 government workers on Tuesday, that government had ignored a 21-day ultimatum which ends on Friday, December 20, to increase salaries and improve conditions of service or face anation wide strike.

- The Public Affairs Committee (PAC), a body overseeing the transition to multi-party democracy in Malawi, said on Tuesday it was dissappointed with the decision of the Speaker of the National Assembly's decision to allow the current sitting of Parliament to proceed without the constitutional two-thirds majority.
- The Japanese government has pledged support to Malawi government of of 786 million kwacha for debt relief and fiscal restructuring and deregulation programme.
